# Active AI Reading

> A course where we read AI papers actively: we summarize, critique, redraw, reimplement and share them, written by the students.

Students of a graduate course read one AI research paper per week and publish what they make of it: rewritten abstracts, critiques, redrawn figures, reimplementations, literature maps, follow-up ideas and social media posts. Each paper page collects everything written about that paper.

## Papers

- [Matryoshka Language Model Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/papers/matryoshka-lm-suites/): Nathan Godey, Yoav Artzi, 2026 (arXiv 2608.09703)
- [Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/papers/cross-lingual-knowledge-pretraining/): Bilingual LLMs learn the same fact twice, once per language, and the cause is largely tokenization: two copies of English with disjoint token IDs already fail to share knowledge. Mapping Arabic words into English tokens (word-wise translation) makes knowledge transfer 14× better. (arXiv 2609.19291)
- [Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/papers/recurrent-depth-latent-reasoning/): Jonas Geiping, Sean McLeish, Neel Jain, John Kirchenbauer, Siddharth Singh, Brian R. Bartoldson, Bhavya Kailkhura, Abhinav Bhatele, Tom Goldstein, 2025 (arXiv 2502.05171)

## Posts

- [Week 1 in one page: tokens keep knowledge apart](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/week-1-in-one-page/): The paper, what we learned, and everything the class wrote about it, in a five-minute read. (Communicate to the world, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Three things to remember, and where the paper hides them](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/three-things-to-remember/): The points most readers should leave with, and how the paper could make them harder to miss. (Writing, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [The paper in four feeds](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/the-paper-in-four-feeds/): Posts for X, Bluesky, Mastodon and LinkedIn, and why each one is written differently. (Communicate to the world, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [The core idea in one picture](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/the-core-idea-in-one-picture/): Same sentence, same model, different token IDs, and the knowledge stops flowing. A diagram of the three setups. (Visualization, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Rewriting the abstract: lead with the surprise](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/rewriting-the-abstract/): The paper's most striking result is buried in sentence six. Here is a version that starts with it. (Writing, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Reimplementing CLeq: what does 12.6% actually mean?](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/reimplementing-cleq/): I simulated the paper's measurement with a known amount of transfer. The metric is right at 0% and 100%, and generous in between. (Coding, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Where this paper comes from: a literature map](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/literature-map/): The four lines of work it builds on, and the one it argues with. (Research skills, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Five follow-ups worth doing](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/follow-ups-worth-doing/): Concrete next experiments, from a weekend project to a thesis chapter, and why each is worth the time. (Research skills, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Fictive facts: how to know exactly what a model saw](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/fictive-facts/): A five-minute lesson on the trick that makes controlled knowledge experiments in pretraining possible. (Learning to learn, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [Critique: a clean diagnosis, a partial cure](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/critique/): Strengths, weaknesses, what would have made it stronger, and a verdict. (Research skills, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
- [A better Figure 2: the threshold the bar chart hides](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/a-better-figure-2/): The paper's key soft-mapping result is a curve with a cliff. Drawn as bars, the cliff disappears. (Visualization, on "Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge", 2026-10-16)
